questions.question: Which of the following provisions of the Indian constitution is borrowed from the constitution of Canada?
questions.solution: The Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (Article 143) is borrowed from the Constitution of Canada. Under this provision, the President can seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on matters of public importance. Other Canadian features: A quasi-federal form of government (a strong centre), vesting of residuary powers in the Centre, and the appointment of State Governors by the Centre.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution mentions that it is duty of the Union government to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance?
questions.solution: Article 355 of the Indian Constitution imposes a duty on the Union Government to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance. It also ensures that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. Note: This article often serves as a precursor or justification for the imposition of President's Rule under Article 356.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution is related to the writ of the High Courts?
questions.solution: Article 226 empowers the High Courts to issue writs (such as Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, etc.) for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other legal purpose. Comparison: While Article 32 gives similar powers to the Supreme Court, the writ jurisdiction of the High Court is considered wider because it covers non-fundamental legal rights as well.

questions.question: Which of the following comes under Union List of 7th schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.option_2: Establishment of standards of weight and measure
questions.solution: The Establishment of standards of weight and measure falls under the Union List (Entry 50) of the 7th Schedule. Corrections: Public order, Hospitals and dispensaries, and Public health and sanitation are all subjects found in the State List, as they are primarily the responsibility of local state administrations.

questions.question: The preamble of the Indian constitution is borrowed from the constitution of ______.
questions.solution: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America. While the concept of a Preamble came from the US, the language and ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity were influenced by the French Constitution, and the 'Objectives Resolution' drafted by Nehru provided its core structure.

questions.question: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 of the Indian constitution has added which of the following in the preamble to the constitution?
questions.solution: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added three new words to the Preamble: Secular, Socialist, and Integrity. Prior to this, the Preamble described India as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'. Key Fact: This is the only time the Preamble of India has been amended.

questions.question: Article 2 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
questions.option_1: Alteration of names of existing states
questions.option_2: Admission or establishment of new states
questions.option_3: Alteration of areas of existing states
questions.option_4: Name and territory of the Union
questions.solution: Article 2 of the Indian Constitution relates to the admission or establishment of new states that were not previously part of the Union of India (e.g., the admission of Sikkim). Distinction: Article 3 deals with the internal reorganization of existing states, such as changing names, boundaries, or areas of states like Telangana or Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Which of the following comes under the part IX of the Indian constitution?
questions.option_3: Relations between the Union and the States
questions.solution: The Panchayats are covered under Part IX of the Indian Constitution (Articles 243 to 243-O). This part was constitutionalized by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992. Note: The Scheduled and Tribal Areas are in Part X, and Relations between Union and States are in Part XI.

questions.question: Provisions as to disqualification on ground of defection are mentioned under which schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution: The 10th Schedule, often called the Anti-Defection Law, contains provisions regarding the disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of defection. It was added to the Constitution by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 to provide stability to governments.

questions.question: Which of the following do/does NOT come under Union list of seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.option_4: Audit of the accounts of the states
questions.solution: Intoxicating liquors (Entry 8) is a subject in the State List, which is why individual states (like Bihar or Gujarat) have the power to implement liquor bans. Union List items: Banking, Post and telegraphs, and the Audit of state accounts are all controlled by the Central Government.

questions.question: In which year was the Dowry Prohibition Act passed in India?
questions.solution: The Dowry Prohibition Act was passed in India in 1961. It was enacted to prohibit the giving or taking of dowry and to protect women from harassment related to dowry demands. Note: It was the first time in independent India that a joint session of Parliament was called to pass a bill.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with the Separation of judiciary from executive?
questions.solution: Article 50 (a Directive Principle) directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State. This is essential to ensure the impartiality and independence of the judicial process. Note: Article 51 deals with the promotion of international peace.

questions.question: In which year was the Arms Act passed in India?
questions.solution: The Arms Act was passed in India in 1959. It consolidated and amended the law relating to arms and ammunition to curb illegal weapons and maintain public order. It replaced the older Indian Arms Act of 1878.

questions.question: From which country's constitution no feature has been taken in the constitution of India?
questions.solution: No features of the Indian Constitution have been taken from the Constitution of China. The Indian Constitution is often called a 'bag of borrowings,' having integrated features from the UK, USA, Ireland, Canada, France, USSR, Germany, South Africa, Japan, and Australia, but China was not a source of inspiration for its framework.

questions.question: Which among the following issues are abolished by the Article 17 of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution abolishes 'Untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. The enforcement of any disability arising out of Untouchability is a punishable offence in accordance with the law. Context: This is one of the few Fundamental Rights that is absolute and has no exceptions.

questions.question: Who founded Trinamool Congress in 1998 and became its Chairperson, after separating from the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution: Mamata Banerjee founded the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) on January 1, 1998, after breaking away from the Indian National Congress. She has served as the party's Chairperson since its inception and became the Chief Minister of West Bengal in 2011.

questions.question: Which article of the constitution of India is related to Comptroller and Auditor General of India Audit reports?
questions.solution: Article 151 mandates that the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) must submit audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union to the President, and reports relating to the State to the Governor. Context: Article 148 establishes the office of the CAG, while Article 151 ensures parliamentary oversight through these reports.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned in state list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution: Betting and gambling (Entry 34) is mentioned in the State List of the Seventh Schedule. Union List items: Railways, Inter-state trade and commerce, and Post office saving banks are all under the jurisdiction of the Union Government.

questions.question: In which of the following articles of the Indian constitution is the procedure for impeachment of the President of India mentioned?
questions.solution: Article 61 of the Indian Constitution details the procedure for the impeachment of the President. The President can only be removed for 'violation of the Constitution'. The resolution must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of each House of Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Act added the Right to Education to the Indian constitution?
questions.solution: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right under Article 21A. It mandates that the State provide free and compulsory education to all children between 6 and 14 years of age.

questions.question: In which part of the Indian constitution are the provisions related to panchayat mentioned?
questions.solution: Provisions related to Panchayats are mentioned in Part IX of the Indian Constitution. Distinction: Part IX-A deals with Municipalities and Part IX-B deals with Co-operative Societies.

questions.question: The concept of “Procedure Established by Law” in the Indian constitution is borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.solution: The concept of “Procedure Established by Law” was borrowed from the Japanese Constitution. Note: This is slightly different from the US concept of 'Due Process of Law,' although Indian courts have largely merged the two through judicial interpretations of Article 21.

questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution is related with the Fundamental rights?
questions.solution: Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) is related to Fundamental Rights. These rights are considered essential for the protection of individuals' liberties and are legally enforceable by the courts.
